import re
import pytest
from target import url_basename

def old_url_basename(url):
    """Reference implementation using the original regex."""
    m = re.match(r'(?:https?:|)//[^/]+/(?:[^?#]+/)?([^/?#]+)/?(?:[?#]|$)', url)
    if not m:
        return u''
    return m.group(1)

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url",
    [
        # simple paths
        "http://example.com/path/to/resource",
        "https://example.com/path/to/resource/",
        "https://example.com/path/to/resource?foo=bar",
        "https://example.com/path/to/resource#section",
        "https://example.com/path/to/resource?foo=bar#section",
        # root and empty paths
        "https://example.com/",
        "http://example.com",
        # protocol‑relative URLs
        "//example.com/path/resource",
        # ports and userinfo
        "http://example.com:8080/path/resource",
        "http://user:pass@example.com/path/resource",
        # multiple intermediate segments
        "http://example.com/a/b/c/d",
        # segment that contains a slash (old regex allowed this)
        "http://example.com/foo/bar/baz",
        # query/fragment without trailing slash
        "http://example.com/foo?x=1",
        "http://example.com/foo#anchor",
        # trailing slash with query
        "http://example.com/foo/?x=1",
        # double slash in path (should be treated as empty segment)
        "http://example.com//foo",
    ],
)
def test_url_basename_behaviour_matches_old(url):
    assert url_basename(url) == old_url_basename(url)
